About Anam

A little about me.
A lot about curiosity.

I’m Anam Khan, a journalist with BNN Bloomberg. My work begins with listening—and following the questions that deserve an answer.

Anam Khan · Journalist

Seeing the world through many lenses

I spent my early childhood in Saudi Arabia and grew up in Canada. We moved often, from city to city and country to country, in search of a better life and a solid education.

Those early years shaped how I see the world. Starting over taught me to listen closely, ask questions and look for the stories that are easily overlooked. My curiosity about people and culture began long before I picked up a microphone or stepped into a newsroom.

From local news to national conversations

After completing a Bachelor of Arts at the University of Toronto and a postgraduate journalism certificate at Humber College, I spent several years reporting in Guelph. I wrote more than a thousand stories about the people, challenges and connections that shape a community.

One story has stayed with me: after reading an article I wrote, a stranger donated part of his liver to a baby and saved the child’s life. It remains a powerful reminder of the difference a local story can make. Read the story of baby Matthew and Derek Roy ↗

In Halifax, Nova Scotia, I moved into television and radio reporting for CBC, covering everything from breaking news to longer features. I later returned to Toronto and the pace of a busy newsroom, where tight deadlines made clarity and accuracy especially important.

Across communities and formats

Each move across Canada has deepened my understanding of the country’s communities and cultures. My portfolio brings together television, radio and digital work, including reporting published by CBC News, BNN Bloomberg, CTV News and GuelphToday. I now report for BNN Bloomberg.

Some of the most powerful stories I’ve found have come from the most ordinary places.
